questions.q: May one lie for another's sake?
questions.notes: The Cunda Kammaraputta Sutta's witness scene gives no exception for a conscious lie told for another's sake; Mill expressly allows the exception when withholding would prevent great and unmerited harm and only denial can withhold. Opposite rules on the same question, stated in their own voice. At bar.

questions.q: Is the duty to tell the truth unconditional?
questions.notes: Constant grounds the duty in the hearer's right (murderer case); Kant grounds it in the practice of assertion itself and answers the murderer case directly. The two passages answer the same question with opposite rules; the unresolved question (where the duty lives) is honestly stated. At bar.
